description: Backend: add the products.status column (draft|published) via the ADD-only runtime ensure pattern, make new products default to draft, enforce a server-authoritative publish guard, hide drafts from the public catalog, and add an admin-only product-list endpoint that includes status so the admin UI can see and publish drafts. This is the foundation FEAT-002 depends on. Independent of the frontend otherwise.
steps: schema.prisma: in model Product (api-node/prisma/schema.prisma, near max_qty_per_order ~line 160) add `status String @default("published") @db.VarChar(16)` with a short comment stating it is runtime-added (no migrate) and used for admin publish/unpublish, and add `@@index([status], map: "idx_products_status")` alongside the other @@index lines. This is documentation only — the Prisma client is NOT regenerated.

dataImport.ts: add and export `ensureProductStatusColumn()` in api-node/src/services/dataImport.ts, modeled EXACTLY on ensureProductMaxQtyColumn() (~line 613): information_schema COUNT guard for column 'status' on table 'products'; if absent, `ALTER TABLE products ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'published'` wrapped in try/catch that swallows /1060|Duplicate column/i. Then idempotently add the index: statistics-guarded check for index 'idx_products_status' on 'products' and, if absent, `CREATE INDEX idx_products_status ON products (status)` in a try/catch swallowing /1061|Duplicate key name/i (follow the index loop in ensureProductInventoryColumns()). Add a doc comment mirroring ensureProductMaxQtyColumn()'s comment style (column default 'published' keeps existing live rows visible).

server.ts: add ensureProductStatusColumn to the import from './services/dataImport' and call `ensureProductStatusColumn().catch((e) => console.error('[seed] status column failed', e));` in the app.listen boot block right beside the ensureProductMaxQtyColumn() call.
admin.ts productSchema: add `status: z.enum(['draft','published']).optional()` to the productSchema object (~line 72).

admin.ts publish guard helper: add a module-level helper `function missingPublishFields(d: { name?: string; price?: number; category?: string; image?: string }): string[]` that returns the list of human-readable missing/invalid required fields — name empty/whitespace, price not > 0, category empty, image empty.

admin.ts write path: in router.post('/products') (~line 96) inside the add/update branch, resolve the effective status: for action 'add' use `p.status ?? 'draft'`; for action 'update' only set status when p.status is provided. Add `status` to the `data` object for add (always) and for update (only when provided — build it conditionally so an omitted status leaves the column unchanged). BEFORE the create/update, when the effective status === 'published', run missingPublishFields against the resolved name/price/category/image and if the returned array is non-empty `return fail(res, 'Publish ke liye ye zaroori hain / Required to publish: ' + list.join(', '), 422)`.

admin.ts admin list endpoint: add `router.get('/products', requireAuth, requireStaff('products'), async (req, res) => {...})` that sets `res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'no-store')` and returns `ok(res, { products: await prisma.product.findMany({ orderBy: { id: 'asc' }, select: {<explicit allow-list mirroring PUBLIC_PRODUCT_SELECT fields PLUS status: true>} }) })`. This is the admin's source of truth (the only place drafts are listed). Do NOT reuse PUBLIC_PRODUCT_SELECT directly (it omits status); define a local select or spread PUBLIC_PRODUCT_SELECT and add status: true.

catalog.ts public filter: in GET /products change the findMany to `{ where: { status: 'published' }, orderBy: { id: 'asc' }, select: PUBLIC_PRODUCT_SELECT }`. In GET /products/:id replace findUnique with `prisma.product.findFirst({ where: { id: BigInt(req.params.id), status: 'published' }, select: PUBLIC_PRODUCT_SELECT }).catch(() => null)` so a draft id falls through to the existing 404 response. Do NOT add status to PUBLIC_PRODUCT_SELECT (catalogSelect.ts) — filtering in `where` does not require selecting it, and this keeps the leakage test green.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` in api-node compiles with no TypeScript errors.
`node --import ./src/__tests__/register.mjs --test "src/__tests__/catalog-leak.test.ts"` passes with NO edits to catalog-leak.test.ts (PUBLIC_PRODUCT_SELECT shape is unchanged).
`npm test` in api-node passes with no regressions versus the baseline (all suites green).
ensureProductStatusColumn is wired into server.ts boot and follows the information_schema-guard + 1060/1061 swallow pattern.

productSchema accepts status as an optional draft|published enum; the add path defaults to draft; publishing with a missing required field returns HTTP 422; the public catalog findMany/findFirst filter to status: 'published'; GET /api/admin/products returns products including status.
verification: cd api-node; npm install (if node_modules missing); npm run build
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. For FEAT-002 (frontend):

ADMIN ENDPOINT: GET /api/admin/products (routes/admin.ts). Auth: requireAuth + requireStaff('products') — the web api client already sends the access_token cookie. Sets `Cache-Control: no-store`. Response shape: `{ success: true, products: [...] }` (standard ok() envelope). This is the ONLY endpoint that lists DRAFTS; the public GET /api/products now hides them. The admin UI MUST switch its product list from the public useProducts to a new useAdminProducts hitting this endpoint, or drafts will be invisible to the admin.

ADMIN SELECT FIELDS (orderBy id asc): the full PUBLIC_PRODUCT_SELECT allow-list PLUS `status`. Concretely: id, name, brand, category, weight, mrp, price, discount, image, description, features, seo_title, seo_description, seo_keywords, og_image, seo_slug, seo_overrides, seo_auto_json, seo_score, seo_problems, seo_generated_at, seo_source_hash, in_stock, featured, sku, stock, unit, tax_rate, max_qty_per_order, created_at, updated_at, AND status. (DECIMAL fields come back as strings — reuse normalizeProduct().)

STATUS FIELD: products.status is VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'published', values 'draft' | 'published'. Added at runtime by ensureProductStatusColumn() in services/dataImport.ts (wired into server.ts boot beside ensureProductMaxQtyColumn) + mirrored on schema.prisma with @@index idx_products_status. Existing live rows default to 'published' so they stay visible. NO prisma migrate/db push was run (and `prisma generate` is blocked in this env — the worktree keeps its stub client, so the known tsc $queryRawUnsafe-generic / missing-POS-delegate errors are the EXPECTED baseline, not regressions).

SAVE PATH (router.post('/products')): productSchema now accepts optional `status: 'draft'|'published'`. On action 'add' the effective status defaults to 'draft' (the create ALWAYS writes status). On action 'update' status is written ONLY when the client sends it (omitted = column unchanged). So the Publish/Unpublish button should POST action 'update' with `product: { id, status: 'published' | 'draft' }` (plus the other fields the form normally sends).

PUBLISH GUARD (server-authoritative, HTTP 422): before writing status 'published' the server runs missingPublishFields() requiring non-empty name, price > 0, non-empty category, non-empty image. If any is missing it returns 422 with message `Publish ke liye ye zaroori hain / Required to publish: <comma-list>` (list items are bilingual: 'name / naam', 'price / keemat', 'category / category', 'image / photo'). The frontend should surface this 422 message as a toast and keep the product as draft. NOTE: the guard checks the fields in the SAME request payload, so a publish-only toggle must include name/price/category/image in the posted product (or the save must carry the full form) — a bare {id,status:'published'} with blanks will 422.

PUBLIC CATALOG: GET /api/products -> findMany where status:'published'. GET /api/products/:id -> findFirst where {id, status:'published'} else existing 404. PUBLIC_PRODUCT_SELECT (catalogSelect.ts) was intentionally NOT changed (status is filtered in `where`, not selected) so catalog-leak.test.ts stays green (confirmed 3/3, full suite 68/68).

VERIFICATION RESULTS: catalog-leak single test 3/3 pass (no edits); npm test 68/68 pass; build shows only the pre-existing EXPECTED stub-client tsc errors (no new error references status/missingPublishFields/the admin endpoint).
